_note: TYPICAL running watts for common Indian household appliances, used ONLY for the optional appliance breakdown (an estimate, scaled to the home's real meter total). 'watts' x 'duty' is used only when the user types the label wattage (rated_watts) or for appliances with no star data; 'duty' = fraction of switched-on time the appliance draws its rated power (compressors cycle). ACs, fridges and ceiling fans also have per-star values from BEE star labels (see '_star_sources' and 'star' blocks).

_star_sources.bee_guide: Bureau of Energy Efficiency, 'Know your Star Label & Make a Right Choice', Session 2 (beestarlabel.com/Content/Files/Session_2.pdf): inverter split AC ISEER bands (1-star 3.10-3.29, 2-star 3.30-3.49, 3-star 3.50-3.99, 4-star 4.00-4.49, 5-star 4.50+); frost-free fridge annual kWh for 250 L (1-star 400, 5-star 164); ceiling fan service value bands (1-star 3.2-3.4 ... 5-star 4.0+) and a 69 W non-star example. Label tables 2006-2019; newer BEE tables are stricter.
_star_sources.cse_dte_2025: Down To Earth / CSE, 'What is the star rating label of an air-conditioner telling you?', 22 Sep 2025: label annual consumption assumes 1,600 cooling hours a year; category averages 3-star 1,008 kWh, 4-star 903 kWh, 5-star ~740 kWh.
_star_sources.consumer_affairs_fans: Dept. of Consumer Affairs comparative test, ceiling fans (IS 374:2018): minimum air delivery for a 1,200 mm fan is 210 m3/min.
_star_sources.how_derived: AC 1.5 ton: kWh per running hour = annual label kWh / 1,600 (3/4/5-star from CSE averages; 1/2-star = 3-star x ISEER ratio from BEE bands, using band mid-points 3.75/3.2 and 3.75/3.4). AC 1 ton = 1.5 ton x 2/3 (capacity ratio, our assumption). Fridge: 250 L frost-free, 1 and 5-star from BEE, 2-4 star straight-line between them, kWh per day = annual / 365. Fan: watts = 210 m3/min / service-value mid-point (5-star at 4.0). No star given: AC and fridge assume 3-star; fan uses the 70 W non-star typical value (BEE example: 69 W).
